Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates marked tracheomegaly (indicated by arrowheads) and multiple well-defined nodular opacities in the right lower lung zone, along with increased linear markings (bronchial wall thickening/bronchiectasis) at the left pulmonary base (indicated by the single arrow). This pattern of tracheobronchomegaly with lower lobe predominant bronchiectasis and nodularity is characteristic of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome.
